scout.purpose: A design system turns tokens, themes, semantic components, and slot contracts into consistent product behaviour without hiding ordinary dependencies.
scout.realWorldUse: Multi-screen applications need shared colour, typography, shape, spacing, component variants, and accessible interaction policy.
scout.outcome: Create theme tokens and slot-based components, use CompositionLocal for truly tree-scoped concerns, and enforce the system with previews and tests.

blocks.text: MaterialTheme supplies colour scheme, typography, and shapes through the composition tree. A product theme can map brand and semantic roles to light and dark values while keeping components expressed as onSurface, error, primary, and similar roles rather than raw colours. Add custom tokens such as spacing or elevations only when they represent a coherent repeated decision. Dynamic colour is a policy choice and must preserve contrast, identity, and fallback resources. Avoid treating every one-off dimension as a global token.

blocks.caption: Tree-scoped theme tokens extend MaterialTheme without hiding feature dependencies.

blocks.text: Design-system components wrap semantic Material components and expose focused variants or composable slots. Required content comes first, modifier is the first optional parameter, state and events remain caller-owned, and optional slots allow structured extension. The wrapper should preserve touch targets, roles, focus, enabled state, and content descriptions. Avoid a universal component with dozens of booleans. Preview meaningful combinations under light, dark, large font, long translation, RTL, selected, disabled, loading, and error states.

blocks.caption: Tree-scoped theme tokens extend MaterialTheme without hiding feature dependencies.

blocks.title: Implicit is a cost
blocks.text: Use CompositionLocal when descendants conceptually inherit the value, not to avoid parameters.

CompositionLocal provides data implicitly to descendants and is appropriate when the value is conceptually ambient and broadly cross-cutting, such as theme tokens. staticCompositionLocalOf invalidates a wider provider subtree when changed; compositionLocalOf tracks reads more precisely. Dependencies such as repositories, navigation, and screen state should normally remain explicit or enter through app-level injection because implicit access obscures ownership and testing. Give a Local a safe default only when absence is genuinely valid; otherwise fail clearly near the provider boundary.

A production implementation should make this topic observable and testable. Start with a concrete user outcome, then cover loading or absence, failure, recreation, rapid repeated input, long content, large font scale, and alternate navigation entry where relevant. Keep state ownership visible in parameters and keep side effects behind a lifecycle-aware boundary. Use previews for representative visual states, unit tests for pure state transformation, Compose UI tests for semantics and interaction, and runtime inspection only when the question depends on scheduling, layout, drawing, or device behaviour. Document any trade-off that a future maintainer cannot infer from the code. Correctness means the feature still behaves predictably when recomposition, cancellation, configuration change, or user timing differs from the happy-path demonstration.

steps.label: Name contract
steps.detail: State the owner, lifetime, inputs, output, and cancellation behaviour.

steps.label: Implement
steps.detail: Use the narrowest API that expresses the required lifecycle and semantics.

steps.label: Exercise
steps.detail: Cover normal, empty, failure, recreation, and rapid-interaction states.

steps.label: Observe
steps.detail: Use tests, inspection, or traces appropriate to the behaviour.

steps.label: Refine
steps.detail: Change the measured cause while preserving explicit ownership.

blocks.title: Do not hide repositories in locals
blocks.text: Implicit business dependencies obscure ownership, lifecycle, and isolated tests.

inspect.title: Expose the hidden repository
inspect.code:
val LocalRepo = staticCompositionLocalOf<Repo> { error("missing") }
@Composable fun BuyButton() { LocalRepo.current.buy() }
walkthrough: A leaf silently performs business work through an implicit global-like dependency.
Ownership, lifecycle, preview setup, and event testing become unclear.
Accept an onBuy intent and let the route or state holder use the repository.
inspect.expectedOutput: The button is reusable and business dependency ownership remains explicit.

trap_check.mistake: Creating a global token for every isolated padding value.
trap_check.why: The token surface becomes meaningless and difficult to evolve.
trap_check.fix: Promote only coherent repeated product decisions.

trap_check.mistake: Optimising or abstracting before the behaviour is measured.
trap_check.why: It adds machinery while the actual ownership or runtime problem remains unknown.
trap_check.fix: Write a focused test or collect runtime evidence before changing the design.

challenge_intro.task: Create light and dark semantic tokens plus two accessible slot-based components, documenting why each dependency is explicit or tree-scoped.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: Tokens express roles rather than screen-specific colours. Components retain semantic Material behaviour. Previews cover long text, RTL, and large font.

recall.answer: Semantic colour, typography, and shape roles.

recall.prompt: What is a good CompositionLocal use?

recall.answer: Semantics, interaction, state ownership, and focused extension.
